nodes.label: SRP v4 README (restructured, TabR-style project guide)
nodes.rationale: Reorganised into main results → reproduce → understand → research log so a reader gets the headline and the reproduction recipe before the narrative; research log stops at Step 9 (older than v4/README.md).

nodes.label: GPU cluster workflow (edit → sync → run → copy back)
nodes.rationale: Shared university cluster with a preinstalled `srp` conda env (base has no PyTorch); GPU chosen by lowest utilization rather than most free memory because the contention is for compute, not space. The person running Claude Code never SSHes to the server on the user's behalf — every server command is run by the user.

nodes.label: sync_to_server.sh safeguards
nodes.rationale: Refuses to run if hostname says you're already on the server, and backs up anything it would overwrite under ../v4_overwritten_<timestamp>/ so a sync can never silently destroy a notebook whose results weren't copied back.

nodes.label: nbconvert --inplace writes once, at the end
nodes.rationale: No incremental checkpointing, so Ctrl-C loses the ENTIRE run, and a fresh run overwrites the notebook file itself — hence always copy results back before syncing new code, and detach long runs with nohup/disown.

nodes.label: Per-module [PASS]/[FAIL] self-tests
nodes.rationale: Every core module runs its own checks under __main__ (weak_learners, attention, embeddings, feature_gating, model) with no GPU needed, so the environment and code can be verified in seconds before any notebook result is trusted.

nodes.label: SRP_* environment-variable overrides
nodes.rationale: SRP_SUBSAMPLE/TRIALS/TRIAL_EPOCHS/FINAL_EPOCHS/FINAL_SEEDS/JOBS/KEY/ARM let a headless smoke test shrink any notebook to under a minute with no code edits — the numbers are meaningless, every cell running error-free is the point before committing to a 1.5h GPU run.

nodes.label: Feature subsets frozen at construction
nodes.rationale: v1 resampled subsets every epoch, which quietly changes what each expert 'means' over time and makes per-expert diagnostics uninterpretable; v4 draws them once from a seed and keeps them for the model's lifetime.

nodes.label: Identical expert init across arms (make_arm forked RNG)
nodes.rationale: make_arm() builds the weak-learner ensemble first and runs capacity-matching math under a forked RNG, so for a fixed seed every arm starts from bit-identical expert weights — this is what makes per-seed PAIRED comparisons valid, not just averages.

nodes.label: Chunked GPU evaluation
nodes.rationale: training.py's evaluate()/predict() process val/test in 4096-row batches to avoid CUDA OOM when parallel workers share a GPU; verified numerically identical to single-pass evaluation to 7 decimal places.

nodes.label: Findings computed from the run, never hand-typed
nodes.rationale: Each notebook's closing Findings section is Python reading study.best_params / a results DataFrame, specifically so a stale or wrong number cannot survive a copy-paste.

nodes.label: Timestamped progress logs under runs/
nodes.rationale: runs/<NN>_progress_<timestamp>.log with a symlink to the latest, never deleted on restart, so a crashed run's partial progress survives even though the notebook's own outputs don't. runs/ is gitignored, disposable scratch — except when a notebook deliberately reads one back (notebook 10 reloading notebook 09's Optuna study instead of re-typing its winning hyperparameters).

nodes.label: Two dataset tiers (diagnostic samples vs exact published splits)
nodes.rationale: datasets.py gives small 10k-row auto-downloaded samples with our own reproducible splits for fast diagnostics; benchmarks.py/benchmarks_rtdl.py give full-scale data with the papers' exact splits so results are directly comparable to published numbers. A READY marker per dataset folder confirms extraction succeeded.
